data.title: Image
data.tagline: Display an image with the right size, crop, and fallback
data.description: An image component can handle aspect ratio, cropping, lazy loading, preview, and loading failure consistently. Reserve its space to prevent layout shifts. Meaningful images need alternative text; purely decorative images should be ignored by screen readers.

distinctions.label: Icon
distinctions.explanation: Image shows a photo, illustration, or the content itself. Icon is a small reusable symbol for an action or status.

distinctions.label: Video
distinctions.explanation: Image is one static frame. Video has time-based content such as play, pause, duration, and sound.

use: Images that need preview or loading states
avoid: Stretch an image into the wrong ratio
Load full-size files for tiny thumbnails
Leave a broken-image icon with no fallback
Write alternative text that adds no useful meaning

lessonPractice.title: Product card images have different source ratios. Cards jump taller after loading and some images stretch. How should this be handled?

options.label: Reserve a consistent ratio, crop proportionally, and provide text alternatives for content images
options.feedback: Reserved dimensions reduce layout shift, proportional cropping avoids distortion, and text covers failures and nonvisual reading.

options.label: Give every source the same width and height and let the browser stretch it to fill
options.feedback: The boxes become consistent, but changing aspect ratio distorts products and can mislead visual judgment.

options.label: Reserve no image space and let each natural image size expand its card after loading
options.feedback: Original ratios remain intact, but card heights change during loading and make surrounding content jump.

data.agentPrompt: Use one aspect ratio for product-card image containers and reserve the space before load. Crop proportionally instead of stretching, add meaningful alt text, and provide a failure fallback. Test landscape, portrait, and slow-network cases.
